title: Self-drive wake — plan 001
epic_title: Build the wake capability: batched state reads, the watch loop, and the status verb

tasks.title: Define the reader port, its typed state model, and the conformance kit skeleton
tasks.goal: A consumer-side reader interface exists with its complete typed result model, an in-process fake, and the conformance kit skeleton every adapter must pass.
tasks.current: No port can answer proposal state: the code-host port opens proposals and reads one proposal's checks; the tracker port's comment surface is write-only; landing and comment reads do not exist.
tasks.desired: One batch call returns, per requested proposal ref — always all of them, in order: landing state (open · landed · closed-unlanded · unknown) carrying the medium-reported landed revision id; per-context check states with required-but-missing contexts named; comments newer than a caller-held cursor, surface-tagged; and a typed unknown reason (rate-limited · offline · parse-defect · timeout) where the medium cannot answer. The kit skeleton asserts the all-refs-answered and typed-unknown properties against any implementation, and the fake passes it.
scope: The reader interface (one batch method) and its closed result types, including the claim-marked landing with revision id
The typed unknown model: per-proposal unknowns never omitted, never zero-valued; the top-level error reserved for transport-fatal cases
An in-process fake implementing the port for consumer tests
The conformance kit skeleton (all-refs-answered, typed-unknown, claim-marking) with authoring notes for future adapters
out_of_scope: Any real medium adapter — the GitHub and Carina implementations are their own tasks
Any consumer (loop, verb) — this task delivers the seam and its kit only
acceptance: The kit run against the in-process fake passes: a mixed fixture batch returns every ref exactly once with all three state kinds populated or typed-unknown
A landed fixture result carries a non-empty revision id, and the kit asserts landing is presented as the medium's claim (the ancestry-check fixture consumes it without further reads)
A fixture where the medium cannot answer yields a typed unknown reason — the kit fails any implementation that omits a ref or returns an untyped zero value
Existing executor port tests pass unchanged — no existing interface is edited

tasks.title: Implement the Carina adapter's reads over the local store
tasks.goal: The local tracker's adapter answers the reader port from store records, with the 1-second mtime-scan cadence advice declared.
tasks.current: The Carina adapter opens proposals and writes comments; nothing reads a proposal's landing, verdict, or notes back through a port.
tasks.desired: A batch read maps store records to the typed model — the store's accepted/closed markers as the medium's landing claim with the recorded revision id, recorded verdict fields as check states, record notes as comments — and declares cadence advice of one second realized by an mtime/size scan of the store directories, with zero scanning while unconsulted. Store filesystem errors resolve to typed unknowns, and an unparseable record surfaces a named parse-defect, never an empty-healthy result.
scope: The record-to-state field mapping, fixed against the local tracker's fixture corpus (the frozen design's open mapping question resolves here)
The mtime/size delta scan and the declared 1-second advice
Typed-unknown handling for filesystem errors and unparseable records
The conformance kit run green over the adapter with store-derived fixtures
out_of_scope: Any change to the store's record schema or the tracker's write paths
Any watch dependency — the scan is standard-library only
acceptance: The conformance kit passes over the adapter against a real temp-dir store built from local-tracker fixtures
An accepted fixture record reports landed with its recorded revision id; an open one reports its verdict-derived check states and notes-since-cursor
A corrupted record fixture yields a typed parse-defect unknown — never an empty or healthy-looking result
The adapter declares 1 s cadence advice, and a no-change scan performs no record parsing
key_interfaces: `ProposalStateReader` (Carina implementation), the store record schema (read-only), cadence advice declaration
touches: kit fixtures derived from the local-work-tracker fixtures

tasks.title: Implement the GitHub adapter's batched read
tasks.goal: One GraphQL query per batch answers the reader port for GitHub, per-context and claim-marked, with errors resolving to typed unknowns and the round-trip bound kit-asserted.
tasks.current: The GitHub adapter reads one proposal's aggregate check state; landing, comments, required contexts, and batching do not exist; a rate-limited or failed read has no typed shape.
tasks.desired: A single query covers up to a page of proposals: the merged flag with the merge-commit id (the claim), per-context check runs and status contexts compared client-side against the branch-protection-declared required set (absent protection ⇒ every observed context must pass), and the three comment surfaces filtered by the caller's cursor. The response's error list is checked before any data extraction — a partial or errored response marks all affected proposals typed-unknown; a rate-limit honors any retry-after by deferring to the next scheduled call, never an in-adapter retry loop. The kit asserts a 50-proposal batch completes in at most two API round trips. No REST fallback path exists.
scope: The batched query shape and its closed decoding into the typed model
The required-set derivation with the strict absent-protection fallback
Errors-before-data handling: typed unknowns for rate-limited, offline, timeout, and parse-defect classes
Recorded-response fixtures covering every unknown class plus the rollup-green-with-required-missing case; the kit green including the round-trip assertion
out_of_scope: Write-path changes — the budget is its own task
Any second read implementation — a REST fallback is a refused alternative
acceptance: The conformance kit passes over recorded fixtures: a mixed 50-proposal batch in ≤ 2 round trips with all three state kinds matching the recorded ground truth per surface
The aggregate-green-with-required-context-missing fixture reports not-green with the missing context named
A 200-with-errors fixture marks every affected proposal typed-unknown before any data extraction — no empty-healthy decode
Every landed report carries the merge-commit id, and the ancestry-check consumer fixture verifies from the reader's output alone
key_interfaces: `ProposalStateReader` (GitHub implementation), the batched query document, required-set derivation, cadence advice declaration (≈10 s)

tasks.title: Single-source check derivation: delegate the existing per-proposal read
tasks.goal: The pre-existing one-proposal check read is answered by the new per-context derivation internally, so exactly one implementation of check state exists per adapter.
tasks.current: The existing per-proposal check read computes its own answer independently of the new batched read — two derivations of the same predicate.
tasks.desired: The existing read's contract and signature are unchanged, but its answer comes from the same per-context derivation the batched read uses; the executor's drive-to-green behavior is byte-equivalent on green and red fixtures.
scope: Internal delegation in both adapters, no interface change
Equivalence fixtures proving the delegated answer matches the prior behavior on green, red, and pending cases
out_of_scope: Any signature or semantics change to the existing port method
The batched read itself — already landed
acceptance: Existing executor suites pass unchanged with delegation active
A fixture pair (green · red · pending) yields identical existing-read answers before and after delegation
Exactly one per-context derivation function remains per adapter — the old computation is removed, not shadowed
key_interfaces: The existing one-proposal checks method (unchanged contract), the shared per-context derivation

tasks.title: Implement the shared write budget on the metered adapter
tasks.goal: Every content-write on the GitHub adapter passes one machine-shared token budget that blocks callers instead of ever surfacing a platform rate-limit response.
tasks.current: Writes go straight to the platform; concurrent processes can collectively exceed the published per-minute and per-hour content caps, surfacing rate-limit errors to whichever caller loses.
tasks.desired: A per-repo, flock-guarded budget ledger in the state directory is acquired before every content-write by every pyxis process; saturation blocks context-aware (cancellation still works); a corrupt, unreadable, or missing ledger starts conservative with both windows assumed spent; the caps are named constants citing the platform's published limits; an injected event hook reports deferrals. The local tracker is unthrottled.
scope: The budget ledger (windows, flock, conservative recovery) and its acquire call
Wiring into every content-write of the metered adapter
The injected event hook for deferral reporting (nil-safe)
The burst drill: nine tasks' write sets replayed concurrently with zero simulated-platform rate-limit responses and zero drops
out_of_scope: Any resident coordinator process — refused ground
Read-path budgeting — reads are already batch-cheap by design
acceptance: The burst fixture (nine concurrent write sets) completes with zero platform rate-limit responses, zero dropped writes, and a drained queue
A corrupted-ledger start behaves conservatively (window assumed spent) and recovers on the clock
Existing executor write-path suites pass unchanged with the budget active
Cancellation during a blocked acquire returns promptly with no write sent
key_interfaces: `Acquire(ctx, n)` on the budget, the ledger file schema, the deferral event hook
touches: a new write-budget package under internal/executor

tasks.title: Single-source the wake primitives: staleness predicate and signal grammar
tasks.goal: The existing wake package's staleness predicate and wake-signal grammar are importable, parametrized primitives both wake stacks share — the argus stack's behavior unchanged.
tasks.current: The wake package's staleness and signal handling serve the argus tick with its own bounds; a second consumer would have to copy the logic — the twin-predicate drift class.
tasks.desired: One staleness predicate (age vs bound, with the bound-strictly-exceeds-cadence relation) and one closed-schema signal grammar (identifier + reason kind, nothing else; unknown fields are parse defects) accept caller-supplied parameters; the argus tick consumes them exactly as before with its existing bounds, and every argus-side test stays green untouched.
scope: Parametrizing the predicate and grammar for a second consumer, additively
A property test: the bound>cadence relation refuses inverted parameters
Poisoned-signal fixtures: extra fields rejected at parse
out_of_scope: Any behavior change to the argus tick, its awaits, or its ledgers
The new loop's parameters — they arrive with their consumer tasks
acceptance: Every existing wake-package and argus-side test passes unchanged
Two consumers with different parameters get consistent verdicts from one predicate implementation — proven by a shared-fixture test
A signal fixture with any extra field fails closed at parse with a named defect
key_interfaces: The staleness predicate (parametrized), the wake-signal schema, the bound/cadence relation check

tasks.title: Build the watch loop: await derivation, edge-triggered wakes, completion exit
tasks.goal: The in-process loop derives what a frozen plan awaits, checks on adapter advice, emits instruction-free wakes whose only effect is scheduling a sweep, idles free, never hot-loops, and exits on plan completion.
tasks.current: Nothing runs the reads: no process derives awaits from a plan, notices transitions, or re-invokes anything — the operator is the clock.
tasks.desired: Derivation from durable state alone yields three await kinds — open proposals, claimed tasks awaiting their proposal, ready-unclaimed tasks (immediate trigger); an empty set is provably a completed plan and exits with a summary. While awaits exist, the loop ticks on the adapter's advice, coalesces a burst into one wake, and invokes the injected sweep entry edge-triggered: an unchanged derived state after a sweep drops re-invocation to cadence pace with the worker-wait age accruing — a stuck frontier surfaces as staleness, never a spin. Duplicate or lost wakes converge (level-triggered); restart re-derives with no duplicate effects; cancellation stops cleanly.
scope: Await derivation with the three kinds and the completion argument
The cadence tick, burst coalescing, and edge-triggered sweep invocation with the stuck-frontier downgrade
Idle-zero and completion-exit behavior
Restart, duplicate-wake, and two-loop convergence drills against the port fake and an injected fake sweep
out_of_scope: The CLI verb, the events file, and the executor wiring — the next task
Any claim, merge, or tracker write from the loop — refused by invariant
acceptance: Drill: a transition on the fake reader yields exactly one sweep invocation per burst; identical consecutive derived states never re-invoke immediately
Drill: a permanently-failing ready frontier settles to cadence-paced re-invocation with accruing worker-wait age — call counts prove no hot loop
Drill: kill/restart mid-await re-derives and continues with zero duplicate invocations; a fixture plan driven to completion exits with the summary
One idle hour on an await-free derivation performs zero reader calls
key_interfaces: The loop entry (plan ref + reader + sweep func + clock), the await-set derivation, the edge-trigger state
touches: consumer tests against the port fake

tasks.title: Ship the watch verb: executor wiring, wake events, sweep attribution
tasks.goal: A user runs the watch verb on a frozen plan and the loop drives the real executor, with every check and wake appended to a local gitignored events file and sweep invocations attributed by initiator and scope.
tasks.current: The loop exists as a library; the executor's sweep-start event carries no initiator or scope; no wake-events surface exists.
tasks.desired: The verb resolves the plan, wires the real reader and the executor's public one-shot sweep entry, and runs the loop under terminal cancellation. Every check and wake attempts a typed append to a size-rotated, gitignored events file before its effect — effects never block on the sink, and an unwritable sink degrades loudly via a warning and the liveness surface. The executor's existing sweep-start event gains initiator and scope properties additively, populated by every invoker. The executor's one-sweep semantics and suites are untouched.
scope: The verb (argument handling, wiring, cancellation) invoking the executor entry unchanged
The wake-events sink: typed kinds for checks, wakes, unknowns, budget deferrals; rotation; the gitignore entry
The additive initiator/scope properties on the sweep-start event, populated for operator and wake invocations
The events-unwritable degradation path (warn once per rotation window, keep effects flowing)
out_of_scope: Feature-lifecycle semantics — ownership, branches, e2e stay future ground
The status verb — its own task
acceptance: A fixture plan driven through the verb lands real sweeps: transitions produce claims and proposals via the executor with zero executor-code changes beyond the additive event properties
Every check and wake appears as a typed line in the events file; rotation caps the file; the file is gitignored
With the sink unwritable, effects continue, a warning is emitted, and the liveness surface reports the sink defect
Existing executor suites pass unchanged; sweep-start events from the verb carry wake initiator and the plan scope, and operator-invoked sweeps carry theirs
key_interfaces: The watch verb contract, the events sink and its kinds, the sweep-start initiator/scope properties
touches: the executor dispatch event emission (additive properties)

tasks.title: Ship the status verb: wait ages, thresholds, and loud liveness
tasks.goal: One read-only command shows, per task, what the factory is waiting on and for how long, flags waits past their configured thresholds, and makes a dead or unverifiable checker loud.
tasks.current: Diagnosing a quiet drive means hand-correlating browser tabs; no threshold data exists; a dead checker is indistinguishable from a quiet repo.
tasks.desired: The verb renders the loop's own derivation — per task: state, waiting-on kind, wait age, a flag when the age exceeds the wait-kind's threshold — plus the checker's last-check age from the events file, flagged when it exceeds one cadence, with the defect event firing at the configured bound. Thresholds are closed-parse config keys (review, ci, worker, checker) with the ruled defaults; unknown keys are named errors; an absent section means defaults. Unknowns render with reasons, offline renders the last observation marked stale, an absent or unwritable events file renders a named cannot-verify-liveness defect, and exit status distinguishes rendered-stale from cannot-render. The verb performs zero writes.
scope: The rendering pass over the shared derivation with per-kind waiting-on classification and age starts fixed against fixtures
The threshold config keys with closed parse, defaults, and the shared-predicate consumption
The liveness footer: last-check age, the one-cadence display flag, the configured-bound defect event, the cannot-verify-liveness path
Degraded renders: unknown-with-reason, stale-marked offline, distinguishing exit codes
out_of_scope: Any mutation — the verb is read-only by invariant
Learned thresholds — parked ground
acceptance: The seeded fixture set (waiting-review · ci-running · blocked · stale-wait · dead-checker · unknown · offline) renders every column and flags exactly the seeded rows, with zero writes performed
Threshold keys parse closed with a named error on an unknown key; absent config yields the ruled defaults; the shared predicate consumes them
The kill-the-checker drill renders the stale last-check flag within one cadence and the defect event fires at the configured bound
An absent or unwritable events file renders the named cannot-verify-liveness defect — never a healthy footer
key_interfaces: The status verb contract, the wait-kind classification, the threshold config schema, the liveness read

tasks.title: Reserve the push slot: the hint-only contract and its stub drill
tasks.goal: The push-channel slot exists as a narrow hint-only contract with a stub adapter proving that push can only ever accelerate, never carry.
tasks.current: No push surface exists; nothing defines what a future push adapter may or may not do.
tasks.desired: A deliver-hint interface whose only effect is advancing the loop's next check to now; no payload beyond the hint reaches the loop; an absent or dead adapter changes nothing but latency. The stub is the only v1 implementation, and the kill-stub drill is the conformance bar recorded for future adapters.
scope: The slot interface and the loop's hint handling
The stub adapter and the kill-stub drill
The conformance note future adapters are held to
out_of_scope: Any real push transport — waiting-room ground
acceptance: With the stub wired, a delivered hint advances the next check to now and nothing else — state, awaits, and sweep behavior are unchanged
Killing the stub mid-drill leaves behavior byte-identical to timer cadence — proven by comparing event traces
A hint carrying extra payload is rejected at parse with a named defect
key_interfaces: The deliver-hint slot interface, the stub adapter

tasks.title: Run the proof: a real feature end to end on both backends, with the committed report
tasks.goal: The shipped capability is proven on reality: a real multi-task feature driven end to end on each backend with the contract's numbers distilled from the event streams into a committed report, plus the operator's quiet-state diagnosis drill.
tasks.current: Every acceptance so far is fixture-level; no end-to-end run exists, no report generator, and the contract's ship-rule numbers are unmeasured.
tasks.desired: A report generator merges the wake-events file with the executor's stream by timestamp and computes: operator-initiated sweep invocations within the driven scope (target zero), transition-to-wake latency percentiles per backend against the promised bounds with the clock-offset note, and rate-limit responses attributable to the run (target zero) with read-budget share. The proof run drives a real feature of at least six tasks on the GitHub backend and a Carina-tracked repo, commits the generated report as the evidence artifact, and stages the five-scenario quiet-state drill the operator judges against the contract's rubric.
scope: The report generator over the two event streams with the three metric families and the budget share
The proof-run execution on both backends and the committed report
The five quiet-state drill scenarios staged for the operator's judgment
out_of_scope: Relaxing any bound to fit an observed number — a miss is a defect to fix, never a documented limitation
acceptance: The committed report shows zero operator-initiated sweeps in scope, latency percentiles within the promised bounds per backend, and zero attributable rate-limit responses, each computed from the recorded streams
Read-budget share over the run is within the contract's ceiling, computed from check events
The five diagnosis scenarios are staged and the operator's verdict is recorded against the rubric
The report generator is deterministic over a fixture stream pair — same streams, same report
key_interfaces: The report generator (two streams in, the metric families out), the drill scenario set
touches: a proof-run report under the feature's docs
drill fixtures for the diagnosis rubric
